# Feature: Dirt block — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #90 (Dirt block) from Blocks before it is used in real levels. Effect: Push into void or water to make permanent floor. Unique: the only block consumed to become floor; the bridge specialist. Useful: builds a permanent path the push block cannot. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** push into void or water to make permanent floor.

**So that** builds a permanent path the push block cannot.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Dirt block for the first time in its teaching room (mech-90-dirt-block-room). Teaching moment: First room: two dirt blocks and a two-tile water channel, arranged so that the easy block can be pushed in first but then blocks the second block's path. A player who fills the nearest tile without thinking is left with a half-finished crossing and no way to place the second block, so they restart a small room having learned that dirt is spent in an order and that the order has to be worked out before the first push. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: On land it moves only onto empty floor or a switch plate, exactly as a push block (81)
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Void: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Shallow water and deep water: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Lava: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Fire: it cannot be pushed in; fire blocks it like a wall, because ice blocks (82) are the fire canceller

## Edge Cases & Rules

- On land it moves only onto empty floor or a switch plate, exactly as a push block (81)
- Void: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Shallow water and deep water: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Lava: pushed in, it is consumed and that tile becomes permanent floor
- Fire: it cannot be pushed in; fire blocks it like a wall, because ice blocks (82) are the fire canceller
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Dirt block's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-90-dirt-block-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/blocks.yml mechanic #90.
